subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes are local and unchanged by removing Hⁿ-null sets (reused accepted dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M' ⊆ M ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, x ∈ V, and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P. Suppose Hⁿ((M ∖ M') ∩ V) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Suppose Q is the approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q): dim Q = n, and lim_{r↓0} ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_Q f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Then Q is also the approximate tangent space of M' at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M M' V : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), M' ⊆ M → IsOpen V → x ∈ V → μHE[n] ((M \ M') ∩ V) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–85). In the selected node this locality fact is used through the sibling restrict_im (part (2): the restriction (M ∩ V, θ, ξ) of an IMRep keeps its approximate tangent planes at the points of the open set V). This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.approx_tangent_local-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; the argument below is its accepted proof.
Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; η_r := η_{x,r} = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r; for an arbitrary set A, ∫_A f dμ := ∫ f d(μ⌞A) (Mathlib's set integral). No measurability of A is needed below.
1. Reduction. The condition dim Q = n is part of the hypothesis and does not involve M. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). By hypothesis ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ → ∫_Q f dμ as r ↓ 0. So it suffices to find r₀ > 0 with ∫_{η_r(M')} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ for all r ∈ (0, r₀). The two functions of r then agree on (0, r₀), a set in the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), so they have the same limit (Tendsto.congr').
2. Choice of r₀. V is open and x ∈ V, so choose s > 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ V. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so choose L > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B := B_L(0) (open ball). Then f(y) = 0 for y ∉ B. Put r₀ := s/L > 0 and fix r ∈ (0, r₀).
3. Cutting to B. For every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_A f dμ = ∫_{B∩A} f dμ. Indeed f vanishes off B, so ∫ f d(μ⌞A) = ∫_B f d(μ⌞A) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). And (μ⌞A)⌞B = μ⌞(B ∩ A) because B is Borel (Measure.restrict_restrict).
4. η_r maps μ-null sets to μ-null sets. |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹, and μH[n](η_r(N)) ≤ (r⁻¹)ⁿ μH[n](N) for every N ⊆ ℝ^P (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with a constant c ∈ (0, ∞) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def; addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero), so μ and μH[n] have the same null sets. Hence μ(N) = 0 implies μ(η_r(N)) = 0. Apply this to N := (M ∖ M') ∩ V, which is μ-null by hypothesis: μ(η_r(N)) = 0.
5. (B ∩ η_r(M)) ∖ (B ∩ η_r(M')) ⊆ η_r(N). Let y ∈ B with y = η_r(z) for some z ∈ M, and y ∉ η_r(M'). Then z ∉ M', since otherwise y ∈ η_r(M'). Inverting η_r gives z = x + r·y, so |z − x| = r|y| < rL < r₀L = s and z ∈ B_s(x) ⊆ V. Thus z ∈ (M ∖ M') ∩ V = N and y = η_r(z) ∈ η_r(N).
6. M' ⊆ M gives B ∩ η_r(M') ⊆ B ∩ η_r(M), so (B ∩ η_r(M')) ∖ (B ∩ η_r(M)) = ∅. With steps 4–5, μ((B ∩ η_r(M)) ∖ (B ∩ η_r(M'))) = 0. Hence B ∩ η_r(M') and B ∩ η_r(M) are μ-a.e. equal (ae_eq_set), and μ⌞(B ∩ η_r(M')) = μ⌞(B ∩ η_r(M)) (Measure.restrict_congr_set).
7. By steps 3 and 6, for every r ∈ (0, r₀): ∫_{η_r(M')} f dμ = ∫_{B∩η_r(M')} f dμ = ∫_{B∩η_r(M)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ. By step 1, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Only the blow-up integrals need checking. For f ∈ C_c pick L with spt f ⊆ B_L(0) and s with B_s(x) ⊆ V, and take 0 < r < s/L.
Each blow-up integral equals its integral over B_L(0). For such r, the parts of η_r(M) and η_r(M') inside B_L(0) differ by a subset of η_r((M ∖ M') ∩ V).
η_r is Lipschitz, so this set is Hⁿ-null. The restricted measures coincide, so the integrals agree for all small r and the limits are equal.

subproblems.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to an open subdomain is integer multiplicity (reused accepted dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and V ⊆ U ⊆ ℝ^P with V open. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity, i.e. T = τ(M, θ, ξ) for some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of U (Simon 6.3.1). Then the restriction T⌞V ∈ 𝒟_n(V) is integer multiplicity in V. Here T⌞V = T.restrictDomain, T⌞V(ω) = T(ιω) with ι = testFormOnInclusion. Explicitly, T⌞V is represented by (M ∩ V, θ, ξ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (T.restrictDomain hVU)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: part (2), steps 1–3 of the selected node's proof (Simon 6.3.1, chapter-06.txt lines 733–753, and Ch. 3, 1.4). The selected proof transfers the approximate tangent planes from M to M ∩ V with (IMC)(a); here the sibling approx_local (dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff), called (A) below, gives the transfer at every point of the open set V, so no further hypothesis is needed. This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.restrict_im-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; the argument below is its accepted proof.
Let R = (M, θ, ξ) = (R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient) be an IMRep of U with R.Represents T. Define R' with carrier M ∩ V, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. We check the fields of IMRep V n, then the representation.
1. Measurability: M is Borel and V is open, so M ∩ V is Borel.
2. M ∩ V ⊆ V.
3. Rectifiability: M ∩ V ⊆ M, and M is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
4. θ is measurable, and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M ∩ V ⊆ M.
5. Local integrability in V. Let K be compact with K ⊆ V. Then (M ∩ V) ∩ K = M ∩ K because K ⊆ V. Also K ⊆ V ⊆ U, so ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the local integrability of R in U.
6. ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V), because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono; AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
7. Orientation. By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. A property holding Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. also holds Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem; M ∩ V is measurable). Fix such an x. Then x ∈ V, M ∩ V ⊆ M, V is open, and (M ∖ (M ∩ V)) ∩ V = ∅ has Hⁿ-measure 0. So (A) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ V) x Q, and the same Q still satisfies IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Hence R' is an IMRep of V.
8. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). The form ιω has the same underlying form, so (T⌞V)(ω) = T(ιω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x). For x ∈ M ∖ (M ∩ V) we have x ∉ V ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) vanishes (ξ(x) is linear). M is measurable and M ∩ V ⊆ M, so ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩V} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero), and the right side is R'.action ω. Thus R' represents T⌞V, and T⌞V is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict a representation (M, θ, ξ) of T to (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). Measurability, rectifiability, positivity and local integrability on compact subsets of V ⊆ U are inherited.
The orientation condition transfers: at x ∈ V, removing M ∖ V (which misses the open set V) does not change the approximate tangent plane (sibling A).
Forms supported in V vanish on M ∖ V, so the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ V.

subproblems.title: Mass on W is determined by the action on forms supported in W, across a change of domain (reused accepted dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, V, W ⊆ ℝ^P with V ⊆ U and W ⊆ V, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and S' ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn). Suppose S(ιω) = S'(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Here ι = testFormOnInclusion (V ⊆ U) regards a test form supported in V as a test form supported in U. Then M_W(S) = M_W(S'). M_W = massOn is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm: the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over test forms ω in the domain with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U V W : Set (Euclid P)) (hVU : V ⊆ U) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (S' : GeometricCurrentOn V n), W ⊆ V → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → S (testFormOnInclusion hVU n ω) = S' ω) → S.massOn W = S'.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected node's proof: for an open G ⊆ B ⊆ U the admissible forms for M_G(X) (forms in 𝒟^k(U)) and for M_G(X|_B) (forms in 𝒟^k(B)) are the same underlying forms with the same values, so M_G(X) = M_G(X|_B). This is Simon 6.2.5 (chapter-06.txt lines 228–233) read with the terminology 6.2.16 (lines 335–337: T₁ = T₂ in W). This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_massOn_eq_of_agreeOn (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.mass_agree-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; the argument below is its accepted proof.
Notation. For D ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟ⁿ(D) = TestFormOn D n is the space of smooth compactly supported n-forms ω on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ D. For T ∈ 𝒟_n(D), M_W(T) = T.massOn W = sup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ A_D(W)} ∈ [0, ∞], where A_D(W) = massAdmissibleOn D n W = {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(D) : tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y} and |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. The map ι = testFormOnInclusion hVU n keeps the underlying form (testFormOnInclusion_coe).
1. Put I := {ofReal(S(ω)) : ω ∈ A_U(W)} and I' := {ofReal(S'(ω')) : ω' ∈ A_V(W)}. Since M_W(S) = sup I and M_W(S') = sup I', it suffices to prove I = I'.
2. I ⊆ I'. Let ω ∈ A_U(W). Its underlying form is a test form (IsTestForm), and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ V, so the same form defines an element ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V). Both conditions defining A_V(W) concern only the underlying form, so ω' ∈ A_V(W). Also ιω' = ω, since both have the same underlying form (Subtype.ext). The hypothesis applied to ω' (tsupport ω' = tsupport ω ⊆ W) gives S(ω) = S(ιω') = S'(ω'). Hence ofReal(S(ω)) = ofReal(S'(ω')) ∈ I'.
3. I' ⊆ I. Let ω' ∈ A_V(W) and ω := ιω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). It has the same underlying form as ω', so ω ∈ A_U(W), and the hypothesis gives S(ω) = S'(ω'). Hence ofReal(S'(ω')) = ofReal(S(ω)) ∈ I.
4. By steps 2 and 3, I = I', so M_W(S) = sup I = sup I' = M_W(S'). ∎
(In Lean: unfold GeometricCurrentOn.massOn, apply congr 1 and ext r, then prove the two inclusions above.)
proof_key_steps: Each mass M_W is the supremum of ofReal of the current's values on the admissible forms supported in W.
Because W ⊆ V ⊆ U, the admissible forms for U and for V are the same underlying forms, related by testFormOnInclusion.
The hypothesis gives equal values on corresponding forms, so the two value sets coincide and the suprema are equal.

subproblems.title: Measures agreeing on the open subsets of an open set O, one finite on compact subsets of O, agree on its Borel subsets (reused accepted cmc_ml_measure_eq_of_eq_on_open_subsets)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let μ, ν be measures on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (Mathlib Measure (Euclid P)). Assume that μ(C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ O, and that μ(G) = ν(G) for every open G ⊆ O. Then μ(A) = ν(A) for every Borel set A ⊆ O.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)), IsOpen O → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C → C ⊆ O → μ C ≠ ∞) → (∀ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G → G ⊆ O → μ G = ν G) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ O → μ A = ν A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected node's proof. There μ = μ_X and ν = R_x.measure agree on the open subsets of the ball B_r(x) ⊆ U, and μ_X is finite on compact subsets of U; the selected proof concludes on a half-ball with Mathlib ext_of_generate_finite, and this statement gives equality on all Borel subsets of the ball itself. This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_ml_measure_eq_of_eq_on_open_subsets (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.minimality_localizes-a1.measure_agree_on_borel-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; the argument below is its accepted proof. Write d(x) := inf{|x − y| : y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ O} ∈ [0, ∞] for the distance from x to ℝ^P ∖ O, with d(x) := +∞ for every x when O = ℝ^P (the infimum over the empty set). d is continuous as a map to [0, ∞] (it is 1-Lipschitz when ℝ^P ∖ O ≠ ∅ and constant otherwise), and d(x) = 0 for every x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ O.
1. (Exhaustion.) For i ∈ ℕ put O_i := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| < i and d(x) > 1/(i+1)}. (a) Each O_i is open: it is the intersection of the sets {|x| < i} and {d(x) > 1/(i+1)}, which are open by continuity of |·| and of d. (b) The set F_i := {x : |x| ≤ i and d(x) ≥ 1/(i+1)} is closed and contains O_i, so closure(O_i) ⊆ F_i. If x ∉ O, then d(x) = 0 < 1/(i+1), so x ∉ F_i; hence closure(O_i) ⊆ F_i ⊆ O. (c) closure(O_i) is closed and contained in the closed ball of radius i about 0, hence compact (Heine–Borel). (d) O_i ⊆ O_j whenever i ≤ j, since then |x| < i ≤ j and 1/(j+1) ≤ 1/(i+1). (e) ⋃_i O_i = O. Indeed O_i ⊆ closure(O_i) ⊆ O for every i. Conversely let x ∈ O. The set ℝ^P ∖ O is closed and does not contain x, so x is not in its closure and d(x) > 0. Choose an integer m ≥ 1 with 1/m < d(x) and an integer k > |x|, and put i := max(m, k). Then |x| < k ≤ i and 1/(i+1) < 1/m < d(x), so x ∈ O_i.
2. (Finiteness.) For each i, μ(O_i) ≤ μ(closure(O_i)) < ∞ by hypothesis, because closure(O_i) is a compact subset of O by step 1(b),(c). Since O_i is an open subset of O, ν(O_i) = μ(O_i) < ∞.
3. (Uniqueness on O_i.) Fix i and let μ_i := μ⌞O_i and ν_i := ν⌞O_i be the restricted measures, μ_i(B) = μ(B ∩ O_i) and ν_i(B) = ν(B ∩ O_i) for Borel B. By step 2 they are finite measures. For every open G ⊆ ℝ^P, the set G ∩ O_i is open and contained in O, so μ_i(G) = μ(G ∩ O_i) = ν(G ∩ O_i) = ν_i(G); in particular μ_i(ℝ^P) = ν_i(ℝ^P) (take G = ℝ^P). The family of open subsets of ℝ^P is closed under finite intersections (a π-system) and generates the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P. Two finite measures that have the same total mass and agree on a π-system generating the σ-algebra are equal (Dynkin's π–λ uniqueness theorem; Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite with isPiSystem_isOpen). Hence μ_i = ν_i.
4. (Continuity from below.) Let A ⊆ O be a Borel set. The sets A ∩ O_i increase with i by step 1(d), and ⋃_i (A ∩ O_i) = A ∩ ⋃_i O_i = A ∩ O = A by step 1(e). By continuity of measures from below, μ(A) = sup_i μ(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i μ_i(A) and ν(A) = sup_i ν(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i ν_i(A). By step 3, μ_i(A) = ν_i(A) for every i; therefore μ(A) = ν(A). ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaust O by open sets O_i = {|x| < i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 1/(i+1)} increasing to O, whose closures are compact subsets of O.
μ(O_i) ≤ μ(closure O_i) < ∞ and ν(O_i) = μ(O_i), so μ⌞O_i and ν⌞O_i are finite measures.
μ⌞O_i and ν⌞O_i agree on every open G (G ∩ O_i is an open subset of O), including ℝ^P; open sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, so μ⌞O_i = ν⌞O_i.
For Borel A ⊆ O, continuity from below along A ∩ O_i ↑ A gives μ(A) = sup_i μ(A ∩ O_i) = sup_i ν(A ∩ O_i) = ν(A).

subproblems.title: The space of n-covectors on ℝ^P is finite-dimensional (reused accepted lcn_covector_finiteDimensional)
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers P and n, the real vector space Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ, with its pointwise ℝ-module structure, is finite-dimensional over ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the selected node's proof ('letting α run through a finite basis of k-covectors'); used by the sibling orient_ae_eq. This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration lcn_covector_finiteDimensional (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.support_null-a1.local_carrier_null-a1.covector_finite_dimensional-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; the argument below is its accepted proof. Mathlib provides no FiniteDimensional instance for continuous alternating maps, so the fact is proved directly.
Notation. Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n = (ℝ^P)[⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ. For α ∈ Λ^n and w : Fin n → ℝ^P write α(w) = α(w_1, …, w_n). Addition and scalar multiplication on Λ^n are pointwise.
1. Standard basis. Let e = (e_1, …, e_P) be the standard basis of ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), for instance the Module.Basis underlying the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ.
2. The evaluation map. For each multi-index I : Fin n → Fin P put e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). Define Φ : Λ^n → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)} by Φ(α)(I) := α(e_I). Because the operations on Λ^n are pointwise, Φ(α + β)(I) = α(e_I) + β(e_I) and Φ(c·α)(I) = c·α(e_I). So Φ is ℝ-linear.
3. Φ is injective. Let α, β ∈ Λ^n with Φ(α) = Φ(β).
- Then α(e_v) = β(e_v) for every v : Fin n → Fin P, in particular for every injective v.
- The underlying algebraic alternating maps of α and β are multilinear and alternating. Two such maps that agree on every tuple (e_{v(1)}, …, e_{v(n)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating). So the underlying alternating maps of α and β coincide.
- A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Hence α = β.
4. Conclusion. The index set Fin n → Fin P is finite (P^n elements). So the codomain ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)} is a finite product of copies of ℝ and is finite-dimensional. A vector space with an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective). By steps 2 and 3, FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n) holds.
proof_key_steps: Define the linear evaluation map Φ : Λ^n → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)}, Φ(α)(I) = α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}), on standard-basis tuples.
Φ is injective: alternating maps that agree on basis tuples are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating), and toAlternatingMap is injective.
The codomain is finite-dimensional, so FiniteDimensional.of_injective gives FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n).

subproblems.title: Basic properties of the weight measure θHᵏ⌞M of an IMRep: absolute continuity both ways, formula on Borel sets, local finiteness, and R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P (no openness is assumed) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in W (IMRep W k): M = R.carrier is a Borel set with M ⊆ W, θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W, and ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M; here Hᵏ = μHE[k], R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ (the weight θHᵏ⌞M, contract IMRep.measure) and R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (contract IMRep.action). Then: (a) R.measure ≪ Hᵏ⌞M; (b) Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ (lower Lebesgue integral of the [0,∞]-valued cast of θ) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P; (d) R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0; (e) R.measure(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W; (f) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure; (g) for every k-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P) (an arbitrary DifferentialForm; no smoothness or integrability is assumed), R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep W k), R.measure ≪ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ∧ μHE[k].restrict R.carrier ≪ R.measure ∧ (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ A, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure R.carrierᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → R.measure K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k, R.action ω = ∫ x, R.orient x (ω x) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the identities R.measure = θHᵏ⌞M and 'R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure (integral against a measure with density)' stated in the preamble of the selected node's proof and used in its steps 5–9. They are needed by the selected node itself (steps 5 and 6: finiteness of R_x.measure on compact sets, measurability of ξ_x for R_x.measure, transport of (IMC)(d), and R_x.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure) and by the sibling glue (steps 7–9).
Notation: ν := Hᵏ⌞M = μHE[k].restrict M and g(x) := θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞], so that R.measure = ν.withDensity g by the definition IMRep.measure.
1. g is measurable: θ is measurable (field measurable_mult of R), and the cast ℕ → [0, ∞] is measurable because every map out of ℕ is.
2. Proof of (c). Let A be Borel. By the definition of a measure with density, R.measure(A) = ∫_A g dν = ∫ g d(ν⌞A) (Mathlib withDensity_apply, A measurable). Since A is measurable, ν⌞A = (Hᵏ⌞M)⌞A = Hᵏ⌞(A ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ.
3. Proof of (d). ℝ^P ∖ M is Borel because M is (field measurableSet_carrier). By (c), R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = ∫_{M ∩ (ℝ^P∖M)} θ dHᵏ = ∫_∅ θ dHᵏ = 0.
4. Proof of (e). Let K ⊆ W be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so by (c) R.measure(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ, and this is finite by the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R applied to the compact set K ⊆ W.
5. Proof of (a). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(A) = 0, and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with ν(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ν⌞A' is the zero measure, so R.measure(A') = ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, and R.measure(A) ≤ R.measure(A') = 0. Hence R.measure ≪ ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
6. Proof of (b). First, g(x) ≠ 0 for ν-a.e. x: ν-a.e. x lies in M (ν(ℝ^P ∖ M) = Hᵏ((ℝ^P ∖ M) ∩ M) = Hᵏ(∅) = 0; Mathlib ae_restrict_mem, M Borel), and for x ∈ M, g(x) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (field mult_pos). Now let R.measure(A) = 0 and choose a Borel set A' ⊇ A with R.measure(A') = 0 (a measurable hull). Then ∫_{A'} g dν = 0, so g = 0 holds (ν⌞A')-a.e. (Mathlib lintegral_eq_zero_iff, g measurable). Together with g ≠ 0 ν-a.e. this gives (ν⌞A')(ℝ^P) = 0, i.e. ν(A') = 0, hence ν(A) = 0. So ν ≪ R.measure (this is Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', whose hypotheses are exactly that g is a.e. measurable and g ≠ 0 ν-a.e.).
7. Proof of (f). ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient). By (a), R.measure ≪ ν, and a.e. strong measurability passes to absolutely continuous measures (Mathlib AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac). Hence ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for R.measure.
8. Proof of (g). Let ω be any k-form and h(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)) ∈ ℝ. Put f(x) := (θ(x) : ℝ≥0), a measurable ℝ≥0-valued function whose cast to [0, ∞] is g, so R.measure = ν.withDensity (x ↦ (f(x) : [0,∞])). By Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (for a measurable ℝ≥0-valued density f and an arbitrary function h, ∫ h d(ν.withDensity f) = ∫ f • h dν; no integrability assumption is needed, because h is integrable for ν.withDensity f exactly when f·h is integrable for ν, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise), ∫ h dR.measure = ∫ f(x)·h(x) dν(x) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x), using f(x) • h(x) = (θ(x) : ℝ)·h(x). The right-hand side is R.action ω by the definition IMRep.action. ∎
proof_key_steps: R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ with θ measurable; withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict give R.measure(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHᵏ for Borel A, hence R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and, by local integrability of θ, R.measure(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ W.
A measure with density is absolutely continuous with respect to its base measure; conversely θ ≥ 1 on M makes the density a.e. nonzero, so Hᵏ⌞M ≪ R.measure.
A.e. strong measurability of ξ passes from Hᵏ⌞M to R.measure by absolute continuity.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul turns ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure into ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = R.action ω for every form ω.

subproblems.title: Equal set integrals against all test forms of an open set B determine the orientation a.e. on B
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝ^P open, μ₁, μ₂ Borel measures on ℝ^P, and ξ₁, ξ₂ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k: continuous linear functionals on the space Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k of k-covectors). Assume: (i) μ₁(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ B; (ii) μ₁⌞B = μ₂⌞B; (iii) ξ_i is a.e. strongly measurable for μ_i (i = 1, 2); (iv) for i = 1, 2, for μ_i-a.e. x and every α ∈ Λ^k, |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm); (v) ∫_E ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁(x) = ∫_E ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂(x) for every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B) (TestFormOn B k: smooth compactly supported k-forms on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ B). Then ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) for μ₁-a.e. x ∈ B, i.e. for μ₁-a.e. x, x ∈ B implies ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (B : Set (Euclid P)) (μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ₁ ξ₂ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen B → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ B → μ₁ K < ∞) → μ₁.restrict B = μ₂.restrict B → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₁ μ₁ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₂ μ₂ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₁, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₁ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₂, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₂ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn B k), MeasurableSet E → ∫ x in E, ξ₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in E, ξ₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₂) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ₁, x ∈ B → ξ₁ x = ξ₂ x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the selected node's proof, after the application of the sibling theorem cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, which the selected node performs itself and which yields hypothesis (v) with μ₁ = μ_X, ξ₁ = ξ_X, μ₂ = R_x.measure, ξ₂ = ξ_x: 'For a k-covector α, a compact K ⊆ B' and φ ∈ C_c^∞(B') with φ = 1 on K, taking ω := φα and E ⊆ K gives ∫_E (ξ_X(α) − ξ_x(α)) dν = 0 for all Borel E ⊆ K, so ξ_X(y)(α) = ξ_x(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y ∈ K. Exhausting B' by countably many compact sets and letting α run through a finite basis of k-covectors: ξ_X = ξ_x μ_X-a.e. on B''. Uses the sibling covector_fd.
Notation: ν := μ₁⌞B, which equals μ₂⌞B by (ii). For α ∈ Λ^k and i = 1, 2 put f_i^α(x) := ξ_i(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.
1. Restrictions. For every Borel E ⊆ B, μ₁⌞E = (μ₁⌞B)⌞E = ν⌞E and μ₂⌞E = (μ₂⌞B)⌞E = ν⌞E (Mathlib Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset). For compact K ⊆ B, ν(K) = μ₁(K ∩ B) = μ₁(K) < ∞ by (i).
2. Measurability and bounds under ν. ν = μ₁⌞B ≤ μ₁ and ν = μ₂⌞B ≤ μ₂, so by (iii) ξ₁ and ξ₂ are a.e. strongly measurable for ν, and by (iv) |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for ν-a.e. x and every α (ae_restrict_of_ae). For fixed α the evaluation map Λ_k → ℝ, ζ ↦ ζ(α), is continuous and linear, so f_i^α is a.e. strongly measurable for ν and |f_i^α| ≤ |α| holds ν-a.e. Consequently f_i^α is ν-integrable on every compact K ⊆ B, being a.e. bounded on a set of finite ν-measure (step 1; Mathlib Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).
3. Cut-off. Fix α ∈ Λ^k and a compact K ⊆ B. Since K is compact and B is open, there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ B (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and cthickening δ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper). The open set V := thickening δ K contains K, so the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff for the open set V and the closed set K ⊆ V) gives a C^∞ function φ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support φ = V and φ(y) = 1 for y ∈ K. Then tsupport φ = closure V ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ B, and tsupport φ is compact.
4. Test form. Let ω(y) := φ(y)·α, a constant covector multiplied by φ. It is C^∞ (product of a smooth function with a constant), its support is contained in support φ, so it has compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ B. Hence ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B), and ω(y) = α for every y ∈ K.
5. Set integrals over Borel subsets of K. Let E ⊆ K be Borel. For y ∈ E, ξ_i(y)(ω(y)) = ξ_i(y)(α) = f_i^α(y), so the set integrals over E of ξ_i(ω) and of f_i^α coincide (setIntegral_congr_fun, E measurable). Using (v) and step 1 (E ⊆ K ⊆ B): ∫_E f₁^α dν = ∫_E f₁^α dμ₁ = ∫_E ξ₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫_E ξ₂(ω) dμ₂ = ∫_E f₂^α dμ₂ = ∫_E f₂^α dν.
6. Equality a.e. on K. Let ν_K := ν⌞K, a finite measure by step 1. For every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^P, ν_K⌞s = ν⌞(s ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_restrict), and s ∩ K is a Borel subset of K, so by step 5, ∫_s f₁^α dν_K = ∫_{s∩K} f₁^α dν = ∫_{s∩K} f₂^α dν = ∫_s f₂^α dν_K. Both functions are ν_K-integrable on every s (step 2). By uniqueness of densities (Mathlib ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite, applied to the finite measure ν_K), f₁^α = f₂^α holds ν_K-a.e.; that is, ξ₁(y)(α) = ξ₂(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y ∈ K (ae_restrict_iff', K Borel).
7. Exhaustion of B. For j ∈ ℕ let K_j := B̄_j(0) ∖ T_j, where B̄_j(0) is the closed ball of radius j about 0 and T_j := {y : dist(y, z) < 1/(j+1) for some z ∈ ℝ^P ∖ B} is the open 1/(j+1)-neighbourhood of ℝ^P ∖ B (Mathlib thickening; T_j = ∅ if B = ℝ^P). Each K_j is a closed subset of a compact ball, hence compact; K_j ⊆ B, because every point of ℝ^P ∖ B lies in T_j; and ⋃_j K_j = B: a point y ∈ B is not in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B, which is the intersection of its open δ-neighbourhoods (δ > 0), so y is outside the δ-neighbourhood for some δ > 0, and then y ∈ K_j for every j with j ≥ |y| and 1/(j+1) ≤ δ. Applying step 6 to every K_j and intersecting countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for ν-a.e. y, for every j, y ∈ K_j implies ξ₁(y)(α) = ξ₂(y)(α). Moreover ν(ℝ^P ∖ B) = 0, so ν-a.e. y lies in B and hence in some K_j. Therefore ξ₁(y)(α) = ξ₂(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y, for each fixed α ∈ Λ^k.
8. Finite basis. By the sibling covector_fd, Λ^k = Covector (Euclid P) k is finite-dimensional; let (b_m)_{m ∈ I}, I finite, be a basis (Module.finBasis). Applying step 7 to each α = b_m and intersecting finitely many full-measure sets: for ν-a.e. y, ξ₁(y)(b_m) = ξ₂(y)(b_m) for all m ∈ I. For such y the linear maps ξ₁(y), ξ₂(y) : Λ^k → ℝ agree on a basis, hence are equal (Module.Basis.ext; a continuous linear map is determined by its underlying linear map, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective). So ξ₁ = ξ₂ holds ν-a.e.
9. Conclusion. ν = μ₁⌞B and B is open, hence Borel, so 'ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) for ν-a.e. x' is equivalent to 'for μ₁-a.e. x, x ∈ B implies ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x)' (Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'). ∎
proof_key_steps: Put ν := μ₁⌞B = μ₂⌞B; a.e. strong measurability and the bound |ξ_i(·)(α)| ≤ |α| pass to ν, and ν is finite on compact subsets of B.

For a covector α and a compact K ⊆ B, a smooth cut-off φ equal to 1 on K with compact support in B gives the test form ω = φα, so hypothesis (v) yields ∫_E ξ₁(α) dν = ∫_E ξ₂(α) dν for every Borel E ⊆ K.
Uniqueness of densities for the finite measure ν⌞K gives ξ₁(α) = ξ₂(α) ν-a.e. on K; a countable compact exhaustion of B extends this to ν-a.e.
Testing on a finite basis of the finite-dimensional covector space (covector_fd) gives ξ₁ = ξ₂ ν-a.e., i.e. μ₁-a.e. on B.

subproblems.title: Gluing: a current with a mass representation that agrees locally with integer multiplicity representations is integer multiplicity (IM is local)
subproblems.statement: Assume (IMC)(a), passed as a hypothesis: the exact first conjunct of the frozen statement of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (hypothesis (IMC) of the selected node), namely: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x iff it is one of M' at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt). Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k), μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k) such that μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Suppose every x ∈ U lies in an open set W ⊆ U on which there is an IMRep R in W (IMRep W k) with μ⌞W = R.measure (the weight θ_R Hᵏ⌞M_R) and ξ(y) = R.orient(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W. Then X is integer multiplicity in U (IsIntegerMultiplicity X).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, X ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ) → (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep W k), IsOpen W ∧ x ∈ W ∧ W ⊆ U ∧ μ.restrict W = R.measure ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, y ∈ W → ξ y = R.orient y) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7–9 of the selected node's proof (the gluing in Part I, T4 of the grandparent proof; Simon 6.3.1, chapter-06.txt lines 733–753, and the localization remark 8.3(1), lines 2311–2317). The selected proof equips the glued carrier with the local orientations ξ_{x_i}; since the hypotheses give ξ = ξ_{x_i} a.e. on each piece, we use ξ itself as the glued orientation, which reduces the representation step to an identity of measures. Uses the sibling imrep_measure. Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]; for an IMRep R write M_R, θ_R, ξ_R for R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient. By imrep_measure, for every IMRep R (in any set): (b) Hᵏ⌞M_R ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M_R∩A} θ_R dHᵏ for every Borel A; (g) R.action ω = ∫ ξ_R(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) for every k-form ω.
1. The case U = ∅. Then μ(ℝ^P) = μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, so X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = 0 for every ω. The IMRep in U with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents X: ∅ is Borel, ∅ ⊆ U, ∅ is countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero), the multiplicity is measurable, the positivity condition is vacuous, every integral over ∅ is 0 (this gives local integrability and action 0 = X(ω)), and Hᵏ⌞∅ = 0, so the measurability and orientation conditions hold trivially. From now on U ≠ ∅.
2. Countable subcover. For each x ∈ U choose an open W_x ⊆ U with x ∈ W_x and an IMRep R_x in W_x as in the hypothesis. The open sets W_x (x ∈ U) cover U and ℝ^P is second countable, so there is a countable set T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). T ≠ ∅ because U ≠ ∅, so T = {x_0, x_1, x_2, …} for a sequence (x_i)_{i∈ℕ} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range; repetitions allowed). Write W_i := W_{x_i}, R_i := R_{x_i}, and M_i, θ_i, ξ_i for the carrier, multiplicity and orientation of R_i. Then each W_i is open, W_i ⊆ U, ⋃_i W_i = U, M_i ⊆ W_i, μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, and ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i.
3. Disjoint pieces. Put A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j (Mathlib disjointed). The A_i are Borel, pairwise disjoint, A_i ⊆ W_i, and ⋃_i A_i = ⋃_i W_i = U.
4. Glued data. Let M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and define θ : ℝ^P → ℕ by θ(y) := θ_i(y) if y ∈ A_i (the index i is unique) and θ(y) := 0 if y ∉ U (for instance θ(y) := θ_{n(y)}(y) with n(y) the least n such that y ∈ A_n, Nat.find, and θ(y) := 0 if there is no such n). Then: (i) M is Borel and M ⊆ U (M_i ⊆ W_i ⊆ U); since the A_i are pairwise disjoint, M ∩ A_i = M_i ∩ A_i for every i. (ii) θ is measurable: it takes values in the countable set ℕ, and for every m ∈ ℕ, θ⁻¹({m}) = ⋃_i (A_i ∩ θ_i⁻¹({m})) ∪ E_m with E_m := ℝ^P ∖ U if m = 0 and E_m := ∅ otherwise, a countable union of Borel sets (Mathlib measurable_to_countable'). (iii) θ = θ_i on A_i; in particular θ(y) = θ_i(y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ M_i ∩ A_i, so θ ≥ 1 on M. (iv) M is countably k-rectifiable: each M_i ∩ A_i ⊆ M_i is (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono), and so is the countable union (countablyRectifiable_iUnion).
5. The measure identity μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ. Let S be Borel. The sets S ∩ A_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint with union S ∩ U, and μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0. Since S ∩ A_i ⊆ W_i and μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, μ(S ∩ A_i) = μ(S ∩ A_i ∩ W_i) = R_i.measure(S ∩ A_i). Using imrep_measure (c) for R_i, then (i) and (iii): μ(S) = μ(S ∩ U) = Σ_i μ(S ∩ A_i) = Σ_i R_i.measure(S ∩ A_i) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i ∩ S ∩ A_i} θ_i dHᵏ = Σ_i ∫_{M ∩ S ∩ A_i} θ dHᵏ = ∫_{M∩S} θ dHᵏ, the last step by countable additivity of the lower integral over the pairwise disjoint Borel sets M ∩ S ∩ A_i, whose union is M ∩ S because M ⊆ U = ⋃_i A_i (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion). Finally ∫_{M∩S} θ dHᵏ = ((Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ)(S) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal, so μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ.
6. Consequences. (a) For compact K ⊆ U (closed, hence Borel), ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = μ(K) < ∞ by step 5. (b) Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. (c) θ ≠ 0 holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. (θ ≥ 1 on M, and Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. point lies in the Borel set M), so Hᵏ⌞M ≪ (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ = μ (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous'). (d) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac with (c)).
7. Orientation. Fix i and put N_i := M_i ∩ A_i = M ∩ A_i (Borel). (α) By the field orients of R_i, for Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i(y)) Q; since N_i ⊆ M_i this holds for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). (β) By hypothesis ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i, i.e. for (μ⌞W_i)-a.e. y (ae_restrict_iff', W_i Borel), i.e. for R_i.measure-a.e. y. By imrep_measure (b), Hᵏ⌞M_i ≪ R_i.measure, so ξ = ξ_i holds Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e., hence Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. (γ) Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set W_i to the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M_i ⊆ W_i. Its local finiteness hypothesis holds: for compact K ⊆ W_i, Hᵏ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHᵏ < ∞, because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i and R_i is locally integrable in W_i (field locallyIntegrable_mult). So for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i y Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i y Q. (δ) Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set U to the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M ⊆ U, with local finiteness from 6(b): for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i y Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q. Intersecting these four full-measure sets: for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y, the subspace Q from (α) is an approximate tangent space of N_i at y by (γ), hence of M at y by (δ), and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q holds because ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) by (β). Since M = ⋃_i N_i is a countable union, the property 'there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q' holds for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. y (Mathlib ae_restrict_iUnion_iff).
8. The glued IMRep. R := (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U: measurableSet_carrier and carrier_subset by 4(i), rectifiable by 4(iv), measurable_mult by 4(ii), mult_pos by 4(iii), locallyIntegrable_mult by 6(a), aestronglyMeasurable_orient by 6(d), and orients by step 7. By definition R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, which equals μ by step 5.
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), imrep_measure (g) applied to R gives R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = X(ω). So R represents X, and X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: If U = ∅ then μ = 0 and the empty IMRep represents X.
Choose the local data (W_x, R_x); by Lindelöf take a countable subcover (W_i) and the disjoint Borel pieces A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j, which cover U.
Glue M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and θ := θ_i on A_i (0 off U): M is Borel and countably k-rectifiable, θ is measurable and θ ≥ 1 on M.
μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, imrep_measure (c) and countable additivity give μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ; hence local integrability of θ and Hᵏ⌞M ≪ μ, so ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-measurable.
Take ξ as glued orientation: ξ = ξ_i Hᵏ-a.e. on M_i ∩ A_i (imrep_measure (b)), and (IMC)(a) in W_i and in U shows that the approximate tangent spaces of M_i, M_i ∩ A_i and M agree a.e. there.
R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω) by imrep_measure (g), so X is integer multiplicity.
